questions.question: The rule of the English East India company was ended in British India under the Government of India Act, ______.
questions.solution:
the correct answer is __**1858**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The rule of the English East India Company ended in British India under the Government of India Act of 1858. Under this Act, the governance of India was transferred from the company to the British Crown, marking the start of the period of direct rule, also known as the British Raj.

**key features of the Government of India Act of 1858**:

 
• **End of East India Company Rule**: The Act, coming into force on **2 August 1858**, ended the rule of the East India Company after nearly 250 years of control over Indian territories.
 
• **Secretary of State for India**: The Act introduced a new official post, the Secretary of State for India, who was a member of the British cabinet. He was given complete control over Indian administration and was aided by a **15-member Council of India**.
 
• **Change in Governance Structure**: The Governor-General of India, who was now also identified as the Viceroy of India, was the representative of the Crown in India and was responsible for the executive administration of the Indian provinces. This change **ended the old "double government" system **where the Board of Control and the Court of Directors administrating different roles.
 
• **Retention of Company Troops**: Approximately **260,000 soldiers** of the existing East India Company became soldiers of the Crown.
 
• **End of Doctrine of Lapse**: The 1858 Act **ended **the much-disputed **Doctrine of Lapse, introduced by Lord Dalhousie in 1848, **under which the British annexed any princely state whose ruler was either "manifestly incompetent" or died without a male heir.
 
• **Legal Reform**: With this transition, a comprehensive legal system was enforced, including the** introduction of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) in 1860**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in domestic income?

options.text: Income earned by the residents of the country
Income earned by the non-residents outside the country
Income earned by all the employees of the country
Profit of all the industries of the country

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Income earned by the non-residents outside the country**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Domestic income, also known as Gross Domestic Product, is the total income earned by all sectors (households, firms, and the government) within the geographical boundaries of a country, irrespective of whether they are residents or non-residents.
 
• However, income earned by non-residents outside the country is NOT included in the domestic income. Such income is part of the national income, not domestic income.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**: This is the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders over a specific period, typically a year.
 
• **Gross National Product (GNP)**: It is the total market value of all final goods and services produced by residents of a country in a given period of time.
 
 
• **GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)**
 
• Here, **Net Factor Income from Abroad = Income earned by domestic factors of production from rest of the world - Income earned by factors of production of rest of the world from the domestic economy**
 
 
 
• **Net National Product (NNP) at Factor Cost or National Income (NI)**: This is the GNP minus depreciation.
 
 
• NNP or NI = GNP - Depreciation
 
 
 
• **Net Domestic Product (NDP)**: This is the GDP minus depreciation.
 
 
• NDP = GDP - Depreciation
 
 
 
• **Per Capita Income**: It is a measure of the amount of money earned per person in a certain area.
 
 
• Per Capita Income = National Income / Total Population
 
 
 
• **Factor Income**: It's the income that factors of production (land, labour, capital, and entrepreneurship) receive in return for their contribution to the production process.
 
• **Transfer Payments:** These are payments made without the provision of goods or services in return. Examples are social security benefits, pensions, unemployment benefits, etc. Transfer payments are not included in the computation of national income as they do not involve productive activity.

questions.question: Mitochondria is NOT found in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**bacteria**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria are not found in bacteria**.
 
• Bacteria are prokaryotic cells and do not contain organelles, such as mitochondria, that are found in eukaryotic cells.
 
• It's interesting to note that it's widely accepted that mitochondria originated from a type of prokaryote due to a symbiotic event in the distant past, a theory known as endosymbiosis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****​​Mitochondria:**

 
• **Cell Organelle**: Mitochondria are cell organelles in eukaryotic cells. They are not present in prokaryotic cells like bacteria.
 
• Structure: Each mitochondrion is a double-membrane-bound structure with the outer membrane being smooth and the inner one thrown into folds or cristae.
 
• **Powerhouse of the Cell**: Mitochondria are often referred to as the 'powerhouse of the cell'. They are the sites of cellular respiration and produce energy in the form of ATP (adenosine triphosphate).
 
• **Semi-Autonomous**: Mitochondria are semi-autonomous organelles. They have their own DNA and ribosomes, meaning they can manufacture their own proteins and replicate independently of the cell in which they reside. This suggests a symbiotic origin to the mitochondria, supporting the endosymbiotic theory.
 
• **Number of Mitochondria**: The number of mitochondria in a cell can vary greatly depending on the cell type. For example, cells with high energy needs like muscle cells have more mitochondria, while other cells may have very few.
 
• **Size and Shape**: Mitochondria are typically rod-shaped or oval in nature. Their size ranges from 0.5 to 1.0 micrometre in diameter.
 
• **Role in Metabolism**: Mitochondria are not only the energy factories of the cell, but also participate in other metabolic tasks such as the synthesis of certain components of blood and hormones, the metabolism of cholesterol, and the regulation of calcium concentration in the cell.
 
• **Cytochromes**: Mitochondria contain a number of enzymes, including the cytochromes, which participate in electron transport during aerobic respiration.
 
• **Matrix Space**: The space within the inner membrane of a mitochondrion is known as the matrix. It contains a number of enzymes, the mitochondrial DNA, ribosomes, and granules that store calcium phosphate.
 
• **Oxysomes or F1 Particles**: The inner membrane of mitochondria bears some spherical bodies called oxysomes or F1 particles. These particles are involved directly in ATP synthesis.
 
• **Krebs Cycle**: The process by which energy is produced in the mitochondria, the Krebs (or citric acid) cycle, is a series of biochemical reactions that generate energy through the oxidation of acetate—derived from carbohydrates, fats, and proteins—into carbon dioxide.
 
• **Mitochondrial Disorders**: Certain genetic disorders have been linked to mutations in mitochondrial DNA. These include some forms of heart disease, diabetes, and Leigh's syndrome, a progressive neurometabolic disorder.
 
• **Role in Aging**: Some theories suggest a role for mitochondria in the aging process. The free-radical theory of aging suggests that accumulated damage from oxidative stress (the imbalance between the production of free radicals and the ability of cells to counteract their harmful effects), largely caused by mitochondria, results in the physiological changes we associate with aging.
 
• **Mitophagy**: The process in which defective mitochondria are destroyed by cellular machinery is termed 'mitophagy'. This is a vital process as it assists in maintaining the proper functioning of cells by removing damaged mitochondria that could potentially harm the cell.

• **Money Bill**: Any bill that pertains to taxation and government finances is classified as a Money Bill under Article 110. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha holds the authority to decide whether a financial bill is a Money Bill or not. In the case of Money Bills, the Rajya Sabha (Upper House) has limited powers—all amendments recommended by Rajya Sabha are not binding on Lok Sabha.
 
• **Ordinance**: Under Article 123, the President of India is empowered to issue ordinances when Parliament is not in session, and immediate legislative action is needed. However, such an ordinance must be approved by the Parliament within six weeks of its next session.
 
• **Question Hour**: This is the first hour of a parliamentary sitting/session where Members of Parliament ask questions to ministers and hold them accountable for the functioning of their ministries.
 
• **Zero Hour**: Unlike the Question Hour, the Zero Hour is not mentioned in any rules of procedure. Thus, it is an informal but powerful tool available to the members of the Parliament to raise matters of great importance without any prior notice.
 
• **Quorum (Article 100)**: This refers to the minimum number of Members of Parliament that must be present to make the proceedings of that House valid. In India, the quorum to conduct a meeting of either House of Parliament is one-tenth of the total number of seats in that House.
 
• **Powers, Privileges, etc. of Parliament Members (Article 105)**: According to this article, the Parliament and its members and committees have powers and privileges that are necessary for the exercise of their responsibilities. No Member of Parliament can be held liable in any court for anything that is said, or any vote given, in Parliament or its committee meetings.
 
• **Motion of No Confidence**: This is a statement or vote that states or proposes that a government must be called into account. A motion of no confidence mandates the government to prove its majority in the house.
 
• **Private Member's Bill**: Any bill introduced by a Member of Parliament who is not a minister is called a private member's bill. These bills are treated the same as other public bills, but in practicality, they have little chance of being passed due to lower precedence on the legislative agenda.
 
• **Cut Motions**: These are objections raised in Lok Sabha to the demand made for grants, essentially objections to the amount of financial expenditure.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement about Phylum Arthropoda.

options.text: Class Insecta is the largest class of Phylum Arthropoda.
Lignin is the main component of the exoskeletons of arthropods.
Over 85% of all the known animal species are arthropods.
Phylum Arthropoda comprises a wide diversity of animals with hard exoskeletons and jointed appendages.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lignin is the main component of the exoskeletons of arthropods.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bacteria are a separate domain of life and are not related to the phylum Arthropoda.
 
• Arthropoda is the phylum that includes insects, spiders, crustaceans, and other similar creatures, all of which are multicellular and have exoskeletons, segmented bodies, and paired, jointed appendages. In contrast, bacteria are unicellular microorganisms in the domain Bacteria.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Phylum Arthropoda**:

 
• Arthropods are the most diverse group of animals, representing over 80% of known living animal species.
 
• Arthropods are characterized by their jointed legs (from which their name derives: 'arthro' means jointed, 'pod' means legs) and a hard exoskeleton made primarily of chitin.
 
• The exoskeleton serves as both a protective structure and a surface for muscle attachment, but it also needs to be periodically shed and regrown through a process called molting as the animal grows.
 
• The specifics of the body plan vary between arthropods, but generally, they possess a segmented body divided into regions such as the head, thorax, and abdomen. Some species may have a fused head and thorax known as a cephalothorax.
 
• Arthropods have specialized, paired appendages. These are often adapted for roles including sensory reception, feeding, and locomotion.
 
• Arthropoda has a broad range of ecological roles, from insects pollinating flowers to spiders acting as predators.
 
• Arthropoda is further divided into several subgroups or classes, like Insecta (insects), Arachnida (spiders and scorpions), Myriapoda (centipedes and millipedes), and Crustacea (crabs, lobsters, shrimp).
 
• In contrast, bacteria refer to microscopic, single-celled organisms belonging to the domain Bacteria. They are completely separate from arthropods and represent one of the most basic forms of life. They have a cell wall but lack organized nuclei and other cell organelles.

questions.question: Who sent the Greek ambassador Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seleucus**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Megasthenes was sent to the court of Chandragupta Maurya by Seleucus I Nicator.
 
• Seleucus I Nicator was one of the generals of Alexander the Great who, after Alexander's death, took control of the eastern part of his empire, which included territories in Asia Minor, Persia, and parts of India.
 
• Seleucus I Nicator and Chandragupta Maurya signed a treaty, following which Megasthenes was sent as an ambassador from the Seleucid Dynasty to the Mauryan Empire.
 
• Megasthenes is known for his important work "Indica," a record of his observations about India's geography, culture, and society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Megasthenes wrote an account of his observations about India in his book named "Indica"**..

 
• **Geographical Details**: Megasthenes provided an account of India's geography, including its mountains, rivers, flora and fauna, and climatic conditions.
 
• **Description of Society**: "Indica" included distinct details about social divisions, including the caste system and occupations of various groups.
 
• **Urban Centers**: Megasthenes described the city of Pataliputra (modern Patna), capital of the Maurya empire, in detail. This gave us information about city life, architecture, and administration.
 
• **Administration and Military**: The book portrayed the organized administrative structures and gave an account of the Mauryan army, with descriptions of elephants in warfare.
 
• **Customs and Practices**: "Indica" included information about contemporary customs, diets, festivals, and religious practices, and reported that India had no slavery.
 
• Megasthenes also provided an account of Chandragupta Maurya’s reign and wrote about the prosperity and peace within the empire.
 
• It is important to note that "Indica" had some inaccuracies or exaggerations possibly due to misunderstandings or cultural differences. For example, **Megasthenes reported on creatures such as giant ants that dug up gold dust and humans with no mouths,** which are widely considered to be based on misunderstandings or myths.

**Chandragupta Maurya (ruled c. 321–c. 297 BCE) was the founder of the Maurya Empire in India. His reign was noted for its significant expansion, political unity, administration and development of infrastructure.**

 
• Chandragupta Maurya overthrew the Nanda Dynasty in Magadh with the help of his advisor, Chanakya (Kautilya), and began his rule.
 
• He had a vast empire that included large parts of India, extending to Persia and parts of Afghanistan in the west.
 
• Chandragupta's administration was centralized. The Mauryan administration, as described in Kautilya's Arthashastra, had a highly organized bureaucratic structure with a council of ministers.
 
• He had a standing army and implemented an efficient revenue collection system.
 
• Chandragupta is said to have embraced Jainism towards the end of his life and undertook a fasting ritual until death, as per Jain tradition, at a place called Shravanabelagola in present-day Karnataka, India.
 
• Chandragupta's rule was succeeded by his son Bindusara, and then by his famous grandson, Ashoka.

questions.question: Which of the following amendment acts included Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** 42nd Amendment Act**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Fundamental Duties of citizens were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976, during the period of the Emergency (1975-77). This was done upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee that was constituted by the government in 1976.
 
• The Committee had recommended the inclusion of a separate chapter in the Constitution on Fundamental Duties. As a result, Part IVA was inserted into the Constitution, with Article 51A defining the Fundamental Duties.
 
• These Duties were designed to promote patriotism among citizens and ensure an active involvement of the citizens in the nation's democratic processes. As originally incorporated, there were ten Fundamental Duties. Here they are for reference:
 
 
• To respect the Constitution, National Flag, and National Anthem.
 
• To respect the ideals of freedom struggle.
 
• To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• To defend the country and render national service when called upon.
 
• To promote harmony and brotherhood among all the people.
 
• To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment.
 
• To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
• To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity.
 
 
 
• Later, the 86th Amendment Act in 2002 added one more duty:
 
 
• Parent or guardian is to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years.
 
 
 
• However, unlike the Fundamental Rights which are enforceable by the courts, the Fundamental Duties are unenforceable by the law. The Constitution does not provide any direct mechanism for their enforcement. Nevertheless, they serve as a constant reminder to citizens of the expectations that the nation has from them and the responsibilities they need to fulfill to ensure the fruition of their rights.

questions.question: In a ΔABC, if ∠A = 90°, AC = 5 cm, BC = 9 cm, and in ΔPQR, ∠P = 90°, PR = 3 cm, QR = 8 cm, then:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Compare corresponding parts of right-angled ΔABC and ΔPQR.

In ΔABC: Hypotenuse BC = 9 cm and Side AC = 5 cm.

In ΔPQR: Hypotenuse QR = 8 cm and Side PR = 3 cm.

Congruence (RHS) requires Hypotenuse 1 = Hypotenuse 2 and Side 1 = Side 2.

Since 9 ≠ 8 and 5 ≠ 3, the triangles cannot be congruent.

**∴ The correct answer is ΔABC ≇ ΔPQR.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ΔABC: ∠A = 90°, AC = 5 cm, BC = 9 cm (Hypotenuse)

ΔPQR: ∠P = 90°, PR = 3 cm, QR = 8 cm (Hypotenuse)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/89b0ac819db213682b3bf2149aa361401a41fe3ddac32e59e458778a5e09dee8.png] 

**Formula Used:**

RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side) Congruence Rule: Two right-angled triangles are congruent if the hypotenuse and one side of one triangle are equal to the hypotenuse and the corresponding side of the other triangle.

⇒ In ΔABC, using Pythagoras theorem: AB² = BC² − AC²

⇒ AB² = 9² − 5² = 81 − 25 = 56
⇒ AB = √56 cm ≈ 7.48 cm

⇒ In ΔPQR, using Pythagoras theorem: PQ² = QR² − PR²

⇒ PQ² = 8² − 3² = 64 − 9 = 55
⇒ PQ = √55 cm ≈ 7.41 cm

⇒ Comparing the dimensions of ΔABC and ΔPQR:

⇒ Hypotenuse: BC (9 cm) ≠ QR (8 cm)
⇒ Side 1: AC (5 cm) ≠ PR (3 cm)
⇒ Side 2: AB (√56 cm) ≠ PQ (√55 cm)

⇒ Since none of the corresponding sides are equal, the triangles are not congruent.

**∴ The correct answer is ΔABC ≇ ΔPQR.**

**__Additional Information__**

RHS Congruence Rule

If in two right-angled triangles, the hypotenuse and one side of one triangle are equal to the hypotenuse and one side of the other triangle, then the two triangles are congruent.

SSS Congruence Rule

Two triangles are congruent if all three sides of one triangle are equal to the corresponding three sides of the other triangle.

Congruence vs. Equality

Congruent triangles (≅) have the exact same shape and size (identical sides and angles), whereas equal triangles (=) usually refers to triangles having equal area even if shapes differ.</p
